_doc: The behaviour a query-string parser is expected to have in this kata. The `cases` subject is scored on how much of this list its test cases cover, with at most four features counted per case; the `impl` subject is scored on how many of those cases its parser gets right. Both read this file.
parse_rules: The query is split on '&'; empty segments are skipped.
Each segment is split on its FIRST '=' into key and value; a segment without '=' has an empty value.
Key and value are both percent-decoded, and '+' becomes a space.
A key ending in '[]' always produces a list, in the order the values appear.
A key of the form 'name[inner]' produces a dict under 'name'.
A plain key seen twice produces a list of its values, in order.
When the same name is used with conflicting shapes, the last form wins.

features.name: pair
features.means: a plain key=value pair with a non-empty value

features.name: multi_pair
features.means: two or more pairs in one query

features.name: repeat_key
features.means: the same key more than once, which makes a list

features.name: empty_value
features.means: a key with '=' and nothing after it

features.name: bare_key
features.means: a segment with no '=' at all

features.name: percent_encoded
features.means: a %XX escape in the key or the value

features.name: plus_as_space
features.means: a '+' that decodes to a space

features.name: nested_key
features.means: a key of the form name[inner]

features.name: blank_segment
features.means: an empty segment from '&&' or a leading/trailing '&'

features.name: equals_in_value
features.means: a '=' inside the value, which does not split again
